report:
Based on this evidence, I should correct the premise: the answer is actually **no**, not yes.

## Research Findings: CoQ10 and Parkinson's Disease Movement Symptoms

The evidence does **not** support the claim that coenzyme Q10 improves movement disorders in Parkinson's disease.

**Early promise, later disproven:** A 2002 phase II randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Shults et al., JAMA Neurology) tested CoQ10 at 300, 600, and 1200 mg/day in 80 early, untreated PD patients and found a trend toward slower functional decline (measured by UPDRS) at the highest dose — but this was not statistically robust and was explicitly a preliminary signal (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/782965).

**Definitive negative trial:** This promise was tested rigorously in the large **phase III QE3 trial** (Beal et al., 2014), a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study in early Parkinson's disease using high dosages (1200 mg and 2400 mg/day). The trial was stopped for futility — CoQ10 showed **no evidence of benefit** on motor or functional decline compared to placebo (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/1851409).

**Meta-analysis confirms lack of efficacy:** A subsequent meta-analysis pooling available randomized controlled trials concluded that CoQ10 did not produce significant improvement in UPDRS motor scores or overall PD symptoms compared with placebo, while confirming it is generally safe and well-tolerated (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10072-016-2757-9).

**Later ubiquinol trials:** A pilot RCT of ubiquinol-10 (a reduced form of CoQ10) in Japanese PD patients over 96 weeks likewise failed to show significant improvement in total UPDRS scores (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1353802015002400).

**Conclusion:** Despite biological plausibility (CoQ10 supports mitochondrial function and has antioxidant properties relevant to PD pathophysiology) and an encouraging early signal, the best-designed, adequately powered trial found no benefit. Current evidence indicates CoQ10 does **not** meaningfully improve movement symptoms in Parkinson's disease.
